findings.problem: The ANR detection now matches ANY android:id/alertTitle whose text includes "isn't responding" instead of the exact string "System UI isn't responding". This is broader than before, but it is scoped to the alertTitle resource-id and the app-vs-SystemUI distinction is made by absence of 'System UI' in the title, so a non-ANR dialog with a different title cannot be swallowed. The risk of a false positive is limited to other system dialogs whose title contains "isn't responding", which on a healthy emulator would be tapped Wait and retried — a benign, bounded action.
findings.evidence: const anrTitle = dump.nodes.find((n) => { const text = n.text || n['content-desc'] || ''; const resourceId = n['resource-id'] || ''; return resourceId === 'android:id/alertTitle' && text.includes("isn't responding"); }); const isAppAnr = !(anrTitle.text || '').includes('System UI');

findings.problem: The app-ANR path force-stops and relaunches the app (am force-stop + monkey LAUNCHER + 15s sleep). This is a deliberate robustness change for degraded emulators: without it, the ANR dialog reappears immediately after Wait, burning the whole 900s timeout. The force-stop is safe because the app-ANR path resets _lastForceStopTime/_appLaunchTime, and the stuck detector only force-stops again after FORCE_STOP_RECOVERY_MS (300s) AND after the global cold-start grace (450s) — so the new path cannot create an infinite kill loop. The exact failure evidence from run 35670332996 is not locally retrievable (GH_TOKEN not set in the Actions environment; no local logcat/artifacts), so this fix is defensive robustness based on the documented ANR-overlay hypothesis rather than a proven reproduction; it is backed by the trusted verification exit 0 and the contract test.
